nameStory: Plymouth rose gentian gets its name from Plymouth, Massachusetts, where this rare wildflower was first discovered and described. The "rose" part refers to its beautiful pink flowers, while "gentian" connects it to the larger gentian family, though it looks quite different from the deep blue gentians most people know.
description: Plymouth rose gentian is a delicate annual wildflower that grows 1-3 feet tall with slender, branching stems. It produces stunning five-petaled pink flowers with bright yellow centers that bloom from summer into early fall. The plant has a graceful, airy appearance with narrow leaves arranged in pairs along the stem. This is one of New England's rarest native wildflowers, found in very specific coastal habitats.

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Bright pink five-petaled flowers about 1 inch across with brilliant yellow centers and white star-shaped markings radiating from the center; petals feel papery and delicate to the touch

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Narrow, lance-shaped leaves arranged in opposite pairs along the stem; leaves feel smooth and have no teeth along the edges

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Slender, upright plant that branches near the top into multiple flowering stems; has a delicate, wispy appearance that sways easily in coastal breezes

idTips.label: Fruit/Seeds
idTips.description: Small oval capsules that split open to release tiny brown seeds; capsules feel dry and papery when mature

habitat: Plymouth rose gentian grows exclusively in rare coastal plain ponds and their sandy, acidic shores in southeastern Massachusetts and Rhode Island. Look for it around the edges of shallow freshwater ponds that dry up partially in summer, often growing with other rare coastal plain plants. It thrives in the sandy, nutrient-poor soils of this specialized glacial landscape.

seasonality.spring: Young plants emerge as small rosettes of narrow leaves in late spring, easily overlooked among other vegetation.
seasonality.summer: Bright pink flowers begin blooming in mid to late summer, creating the best identification opportunity when plants are most visible.
seasonality.fall: Continues flowering into early fall, then sets seed in small capsules before the plant dies back completely.
seasonality.winter: No above-ground parts remain; seeds lie dormant in the sandy soil waiting for spring germination.

funFact: Plymouth rose gentian has one of the most fragmented ranges of any North American wildflower, mysteriously occurring in scattered locations from Nova Scotia to South Carolina with huge gaps in between, as if pieces of an ancient distribution were left behind like botanical time capsules.
confusionNotes: Most likely confused with its relative marsh pink, but Plymouth rose gentian has five petals (not the 8-12 of marsh pink) and grows in freshwater pond edges rather than salt marshes. Remember: "Five petals, fresh water" for Plymouth rose gentian.
contextualKnowledge: Despite its name, Plymouth rose gentian isn't closely related to the blue-flowered true gentians most people know. The "gentian family" includes many plants that look quite different from each other, and the rose gentians are actually more closely related to other pink-flowered coastal plants.
compareHints: Plymouth rose gentian is distinguished from marsh pink by having exactly five petals instead of 8-12, and from other rose gentians by its coastal pond habitat and the specific white star pattern radiating from its yellow center. Its flowers are also typically larger and more vibrant pink than those of slender rose gentian or rosepink.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Marsh pink differs from its cousin Plymouth gentian by having consistently pink flowers (Plymouth gentian is usually white or pale pink) and growing in salt marshes rather than sandy shores.
Slender rose gentian is much more delicate and narrow-stemmed than its relatives like marsh pink, which tends to be more robust.
Among its rose gentian relatives, rosepink is distinguished by its square stem - Plymouth gentian and marsh pink both have round stems.
